children: Herbalife is searching for a new chief executive, as Stephan Gratziani will step down from the company's top role, effective Oct. 31.
Following the transition, Gratziani will remain with Herbalife as a consultant focused on strategy and business development, the health and wellness company said Monday.
Herbalife's board has formed a committee to oversee the succession process for Gratziani. In the meantime, John DeSimone, the company finance chief, will serve as interim CEO.
Shares of Herbalife fell 14%, to $10.74, and have lost about 16% of their value year to date.

Gratziani joined Herbalife as chief strategy officer in August 2023 under an initial two-and-a-half-year agreement. He helped helm a turnaround that has seen the company return to growth, following a challenging postpandemic period, Herbalife said.

"Over the past several years, we have established a clear strategy and strengthened the company's focus on our distributors and the markets they serve," Gratziani said, adding that he believes Herbalife is now ready to enter its next phase of growth.

The succession plan comes after Herbalife said earlier this month that DeSimone plans to retire at the end of the year, with Scott Schaefer, the company's senior vice president of finance and transformation, succeeding him as CFO.

Herbalife also on Monday reaffirmed its outlook for the current quarter and year. The company expects third-quarter net sales to climb 0.5% to 4.5% from the same period last year, while full-year net sales are projected to be up 2.5% to 5.5%.
